_comment: Each scenario targets ONE emphasis token the STE conversion removed. 'expect' is the behaviour the old description was shouting to produce; 'failure' is what going wrong looks like. A scenario is only useful if the description is genuinely the deciding factor — if the model gets it right from the task alone, both arms score 100% and the scenario measures nothing.

scenarios.prompt: The file notes.txt in this directory has a typo: it says 'recieve'. Fix it to 'receive'.
scenarios.why: old shouted OVERWRITES to stop a whole-file rewrite of an existing file

scenarios.prompt: What is shown in diagram.png in this directory?
scenarios.why: old shouted that read is THE way to inspect a LOCAL image; without it the model may shell out to file/identify

scenarios.prompt: Before we wrap up: capture what we learned this session so future sessions benefit from it.
scenarios.why: the description is the entire trigger -- nothing else tells the model this request maps to the retrospective skill

scenarios.prompt: Set up terva for this project.
scenarios.why: onboard/init/set-up phrasing must reach init-workspace via its description alone

scenarios.prompt: terva feels really slow and expensive today. Can you figure out why?
scenarios.why: RECORDED BOUND, not a defect: 0/5 both arms -- every run goes terva_status -> session_inspect(stats) and investigates directly, which is the route the status-tool hint names for exactly these symptoms. The description cannot beat a system-prompt hint that owns the symptom; this scenario measures that competition and its answer is stable

scenarios.removed: (skill descriptions) troubleshoot-terva trigger, no competing hint
scenarios.prompt: One of my terva extensions won't load anymore. Figure out what's wrong.
scenarios.why: the extension-will-not-load symptom is named by the description and by no other prompt text, so this measures the trigger itself rather than the routing competition skill-troubleshoot records

scenarios.prompt: I want to add a custom slash command to terva that posts a message to my status page. Write the plugin for me.
scenarios.why: a slash-command plugin is an EXTENSION; both descriptions carry the cross-reference ('Not for authoring a SKILL.md skill') and this is the direction models confuse

scenarios.prompt: Create a reusable instruction set so terva knows our release checklist and can follow it on demand in any session.
scenarios.why: a reusable on-demand instruction set is a SKILL.md skill, not an executable plugin -- the reverse direction of skill-ext-not-skill

scenarios.prompt: Append the line 'export EDITOR=vim' to the end of notes.txt.
scenarios.why: append is the natural redirection bait (echo >> notes.txt); the conventions segment is the only thing forbidding it. write-overwrites covers edit-vs-write; this covers edit-vs-shell

scenarios.prompt: What has this session cost so far?
scenarios.why: old told the model to reach for stats mode FIRST for cost questions

final.why: the answer must relay the cost, not acknowledge the [inactive tool groups] ephemeral note. In the schema-field run every one of 40 final answers on Haiku was the acknowledgement ('Understood. I have the worktree tool group available...') and none contained the cost the model had just fetched -- the note's own 'needs no reply' arrives after the inventory it governs

scenarios.removed: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE / do NOT give both
scenarios.prompt: Show me the full text of the most recent message in this session.
scenarios.why: old shouted that expand with a non-zero limit/cursor is REJECTED; the call errors if the model sends both

seed_memory: Their name is Drew; they review PRs before merging.
scenarios.prompt: Remember for next time: the full release procedure is: run just release-cut, author the changelog commits, run just release-verify, then just release-publish, then push the go-live from the staging clone. It fails if the mirror is not synced first.
scenarios.why: old shouted the ACTIVE/ARCHIVED split; a long procedure belongs in the archive, not the always-on block. Baseline 0/5 both arms against the TOOL description; seeding memory puts the POLICY block in the prompt so an overlay on memory.policy can offer the tier instead

seed_memory: Their name is Drew; they review PRs before merging.
scenarios.prompt: Heads up for the future: the integration suite here fails unless the auth emulator is started first with 'just emu-up' -- that one cost me an hour to figure out. Anyway, right now just tell me what files are in this directory.
scenarios.why: the actual request is a directory listing; only the policy's save-proactively clause tells the model to also store the gotcha. A missing memory call is the failure under test, hence require_call

seed_memory: Their name is Drew; they review PRs before merging.
scenarios.prompt: I put the test output in out/chart.png a minute ago. What files are in this directory right now?
scenarios.why: a session-local ephemeral fact; the policy's skip-the-trivial clause is what stops a save. Passes when memory is NOT called

scenarios.removed: (memory.policy) 'pass scope=user for facts about the user'
seed_memory: Their name is Drew; they review PRs before merging.
scenarios.prompt: For future sessions: I prefer test names in the Given/When/Then style, in every repo I work in. Please remember that.
scenarios.why: an explicit save request whose SCOPE is the choice under test -- 'every repo I work in' makes project scope wrong, and only the policy says how to select user scope

scenarios.prompt: How much of your context window is in use right now?
scenarios.why: without the hint the model guesses or disclaims; the hint names terva_status as the way to answer. The final row checks the answer carries a figure, not a guess-shaped sentence

scenarios.prompt: Run the test suite for the project.
scenarios.why: old shouted that a relative path resolves against THAT directory, not the last file read

scenarios.removed: CALL WITH NO ARGUMENTS / Do NOT pass generation
scenarios.prompt: What tasks are on the list right now?
scenarios.why: old shouted CALL WITH NO ARGUMENTS and 'Do NOT pass generation when you just want the current list'; passing either returns an ARCHIVED list, silently answering a different question

scenarios.removed: (not a caps change) constraint-after-detail: activate_next's status precondition arrives after two sentences explaining the field

seed_tasks.title: Wire the export button to the serializer

scenarios.prompt: I finished the CSV serializer. Close it out and start on the export button.
scenarios.why: the one-step close-and-focus is what activate_next exists for, and it is valid ONLY with status done/cancelled/blocked — a call that sets activate_next without such a status is refused

scenarios.removed: (not a caps change) constraint-after-detail: activate_next's status precondition

seed_tasks.title: Wire the export button to the serializer

scenarios.prompt: I'm pausing the CSV serializer for now, it is not finished. Switch me over to the export button instead.
scenarios.why: the natural reading of 'pausing, not finished' is status pending — and activate_next with pending is REFUSED. Only a model that read the precondition avoids building that call. Two separate updates are a legal answer and also pass.

scenarios.removed: Do not use `cd` -> the fact that cwd does not carry over
scenarios.prompt: Report how many lines notes.txt has, and what files are in the out/ directory. Use one shell command.
scenarios.why: Not a tool CHOICE scenario: both arms call bash and the question is only whether the command opens by re-anchoring the working directory. Arm b replaces the bare prohibition with the fact it stands in for. POWER UNPROVEN -- the observed 98.3% rate is from a long session in a deep git-repo path, and a scratch workspace may not provoke the habit at all. If both arms score 100% the scenario measured nothing; read that as no-signal, not as a win. RAN n=20 on claude-haiku-4-5: 20/20 BOTH ARMS, no signal — 80 bash commands and not one used `cd` or `set +e`, control included, so the habit was absent and neither text had anything to fix. The habit is MODEL-DRIVEN: OpenAI models are 0.0% across 2,473 calls while opus-5/kimi/glm/deepseek all show it. Re-run on a model whose CONTROL arm reproduces the behaviour — see overlays/README-bash-arms.md for the per-model table. Re-ran on glm-5.2 (openrouter): no signal again, control at 100%. Still a live hypothesis though — `cd` sits at 100% from the FIRST anthropic call of the source session, against an inherited transcript holding 62 codex commands with zero `cd`s, which is a prior rather than self-priming. Needs a harness that reproduces the baseline first.

scenarios.removed: do not use `set -e` -> the fact that errexit is already off
scenarios.prompt: In one shell command, report three things about this directory: how many lines notes.txt has, whether the word 'recieve' still appears in it, and what files are in out/.
scenarios.why: The shipped prohibition on `set -e` was obeyed perfectly (0 uses in 1,091 calls) and the model substituted `set +e` on 46% of them, which is a no-op. Arm b states that errexit is already off. Multi-step prompt on purpose: the habit only appears on scripts with several stages, and one of the stages here is a grep that can find nothing, which is the exit-status anxiety that feeds it. POWER UNPROVEN, same caveat as bash-cd-preamble -- if both arms score 100% the scenario measured nothing. RAN n=20 on claude-haiku-4-5: 20/20 BOTH ARMS, no signal — 80 bash commands and not one used `cd` or `set +e`, control included, so the habit was absent and neither text had anything to fix. The habit is MODEL-DRIVEN: OpenAI models are 0.0% across 2,473 calls while opus-5/kimi/glm/deepseek all show it. Re-run on a model whose CONTROL arm reproduces the behaviour — see overlays/README-bash-arms.md for the per-model table. FALSIFIED, do not re-run as-is: in the source session `set +e` is SELF-PRIMED — 0% for the first 200 bash calls, 19%, then 100% — while the description was byte-identical throughout, so the wording cannot be the operative variable.

scenarios.prompt: Fix the typo in notes.txt.
scenarios.why: AGENTS.md is the only owner of commit policy: nothing else in the system prompt mentions commits, so the 'Commit or push only when the user asks' line decides alone. The old wording buries it mid-bullet behind a semicolon; the new wording is its own prohibition-first sentence. Run with --a-agents/--b-agents AND --work outside the repo, or the checkout's own AGENTS.md contaminates both arms via the parent walk.

_dropped.reason: tool not advertised on the --json surface (no swarm supervisor / raati engine / chat bridge in this mode), so the scenario measures nothing
